slides.title: Problems And Applications
slides.notes: Open the lecture as an application atlas, not as a list of success stories. The central question is how each domain chooses a data object, a symmetry group or deformation model, and a task constraint that should shape the neural architecture.

slides.title: The Application Contract
slides.notes: Use this slide to establish the repeated design move. Before naming a model family, identify what changes are coordinate choices, what changes carry semantic information, what output type the task asks for, and what failure mode appears when the symmetry is mis-specified.

slides.title: Chemistry: Molecules As Typed E(3) Graphs
slides.notes: Emphasize that a molecule is not merely a graph and not merely coordinates. Atom types, bonds, distances, angles, and conformers all matter. A property predictor should ignore rigid motion and atom ordering, while an equivariant generator should move coordinates consistently.

slides.title: Proteins: Sequence, Contact, And Frame Geometry
slides.notes: Present proteins as multi-scale geometric objects. Sequence order carries local biochemical context, contact graphs express folded neighborhoods, and residue frames make orientation-dependent interactions visible. The modeling challenge is to use all three without treating arbitrary frame choices as biological signals.

slides.title: Recommenders: Bipartite Symmetry With Asymmetric Goals
slides.notes: Point out the subtlety in recommendation systems. User and item identities can be permuted within their own types, but the two sides are not interchangeable. The task is a ranked edge prediction problem constrained by sparsity, feedback bias, and changing catalogs.

slides.title: Traffic: Road Graphs Carry Time
slides.notes: Explain that traffic forecasting combines a fixed spatial graph with moving temporal signals. The road network restricts message passing, time shifts suggest shared temporal filters, and the task constraint is operational: predictions must be local, timely, and robust to missing sensors.

slides.title: Vision And Games: Structured Grids, Different Tasks
slides.notes: Compare the two grid-like domains carefully. Images often ask for translation-stable classification or dense equivariant maps, while games ask for legal actions under board symmetries and strategic state transitions. Similar locality does not mean identical readouts or constraints.

slides.title: Language And Audio: Order, Causality, And Soft Graphs
slides.notes: Use language and audio to separate sequence geometry from grid geometry. Tokens and samples have order, attention builds a data-dependent graph, and many tasks impose causality. Translation-like shifts may matter for audio, while word position can change meaning.

slides.title: Healthcare: Heterogeneous Graphs Under Constraints
slides.notes: Keep the healthcare slide grounded in task constraints rather than hype. Patient histories, diagnoses, procedures, labs, and medications form heterogeneous temporal graphs. Useful models must respect type structure, irregular sampling, privacy boundaries, missingness, and calibrated uncertainty.

slides.title: Physics: Particles, Fields, And Conservation
slides.notes: Frame physical prediction as the strictest symmetry test in the deck. Particles and fields live in coordinate systems chosen by observers, so rotations, translations, permutations, and sometimes Lorentz structure are not optional details. Conservation laws add constraints beyond equivariance.

slides.title: VR And AR: Pose Graphs In A Moving World
slides.notes: Describe VR and AR as online geometry under latency. The system estimates cameras, hands, surfaces, and anchors while the user moves. SE(3) consistency, temporal filtering, occlusion reasoning, and mesh updates matter because visual errors become embodied errors.

slides.title: Task Constraints Select The Readout
slides.notes: Use the matrix to prevent a common overgeneralization. The same domain can support invariant classification, equivariant localization, structured generation, or counterfactual control. A good architecture matches the output behavior, not only the input domain, and it should say so explicitly.

slides.title: Notebook Residuals As Sanity Checks
slides.notes: Connect the lecture to the executable notebook. The molecule check verifies distance preservation under rigid motion, the attention check verifies stochastic rows, the traffic graph records edge structure, and the particle event count guards the point-cloud construction.

slides.title: Common Symmetry Mismatches
slides.notes: Warn that geometric language can become decorative when the task is not specified. Invariance can erase important orientation, equivariance can be wasted on scalar decisions, locality can miss long-range constraints, and augmentation can hide rather than fix a wrong representation.

slides.title: Takeaways
slides.notes: Close by returning to the chapter question. Chemistry, proteins, recommenders, traffic, vision, games, language, audio, healthcare, physics, and VR or AR are unified by the same discipline: name the domain, name the transformations, then test the task behavior.
